cases.name: LaDawndra "Dee Dee" Dorece Ellington
cases.about:
"The pastor of Ekklesia Christian Ministries told WLKY News that Ladawndra “Dee” Ellington was someone who truly cared for the welfare of others, despite her own hardships.

In a Zoom interview Monday morning, Pastor Stephan Kirby shared the shock of learning about Ellington’s gruesome murder.

He met Ellington while his church was out offering food and other necessities to the homeless. Ellington was staying at a Louisville homeless shelter, but he said she immediately began helping the group pass out items.

“She was always caring,” said Kirby. “She always had a great attitude.”

Kirby said their initial conversation included talking about church. Soon after, he was picking her up for Sunday service.

He said Ellington sang with the worship team and eventually started serving hot meals in the church’s day shelter.

Kirby said while she sometimes discussed personal struggles with him, she never seemed to let health issues or housing insecurity stop her from helping others.

“That smile that you see on the picture, that's her. That's her. I won't say that was her -- but that's her,” Kirby said empathically. “That's who she is. She is that smile. She is that radiant. In spite of everything that was going on in her life, she still had that smile and was willing to help others.”

https://www.wlky.com/article/victim-of-heinous-murder-in-louisville-remembered-for-gentle-soul-helping-others/34099286#

She was formerly employed as a team member and cashier at Louisville Airport but had not worked there since 2018. According to her Facebook page, Ms Ellington had previously studied paralegal studies at Louisville University and worked as a reservation manager at a car hire company.
https://www.the-sun.com/news/1490439/man-killed-girlfriend-and-stuffed-chopped-body-in-suitcases/
cases.narrative:
He allegedly killed her at their home in Louisville, KY about a month before her body was found and he dumped her torso in Bingham Park on Brownsboro Road. He packed her head and other body parts in a suitcase and tote bag and got on a Greyhound bus to Chicago to visit his parents in the suburb of Markham, IL. His mother noticed a foul odor and reportedly called police after she found the luggage in her garage while her son was out of the house.

His relatives became suspicious when they noticed he was guarding his suitcases which had remained unpacked for several days, police said. He also asked them to buy clothes for him, despite arriving with multiple pieces of luggage.

cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She was a graduate of Beth Haven Christian School in Louisville and attended Western Kentucky University.  She was employed at 18|8 Hair Salon as a receptionist.  In her leisure time, she enjoyed shopping and spending time with children.  She was a Christian by faith."

(Her younger brother Andrew ) Thompson is remembering his sister as a pure soul who loved to live in the moment, recounting her often saying, "Today is a gift, that's why we call it the present." Thompson also has the words "La Familia" tattooed on his left forearm to match the exact same tattoo she had on her right arm. "That's something I get to share with her forever," he said.
cases.narrative: He waited for her outside the hair salon where she worked as a receptionist, and shot and killed her, then later committed suicide.
